summary: The revised target (SHA256 9dbac9e3a36faa9ad0c1a585e0637c72940f1a5320bc12dedc795900ac98913b) closes EOSA-006, EOSA-007, and EOSA-008 without reopening EOSA-001 through EOSA-005. Page IR is correctly a 22-ticket pack; EOS-003→EOS-015 and EOS-005→EOS-013 are now parent-to-child coupled on the same pattern as EOS-002→EOS-010; pin-succession is a governance-only owner-plus-independent-verifier packet with successor retrospective audit and no ordinary-ticket bypass. Grok 4.6 remains mandatory review input, subordinate to deterministic tests, independent verification, and named-human visual/evidence/release authority. No P0/P1 findings and no earlier P0/P1 regression. Owner may accept this as planning-policy review_input only. No implementation or deployment is authorized.

strengths: Mapping table still connects program S0/S1, each P1–P8 plan as S2–S6 then separately authorized S7+, A0–A4 under Page IR/P1–P2, draft E0–E8 blocked from S7 until EOS-002/005/007, grandfathered OBX S7/S8 packets, and section 10 as pre-build governance rather than a third phase language.
S7–S11 remain explicitly not current implementation permission; they become enforceable only after that phase's accepted ticket packet and a separate owner authorization.
Website journey remains first; Agent Studio, browser, collaboration, and appointments cannot become source, approval, qualification, or release authorities.
DoR/DoD keep oracles, rollback, independent review, and named-human visual/release authority; Grok receipt plus disposition replaces Grok PASS-as-certificate.
DoR now also requires the named non-author verifier to accept readiness evidence and every P0/P1 disposition for security, privacy, schema, browser, identity, migration, release, or rollback tickets.
EOS-018 still defers CONTRIBUTING/PR/issue/CI enforcement to a post-acceptance governance change rather than implying those controls already exist.
Section 10 still starts with MPA-001–MPA-011 reconciliation and forbids feature implementation from this document alone.
weaknesses: No dedicated S-stage named license/legal; that work remains EOS-011 plus section 10 step 7 and S3 dependency decisions.
Named reviewer roster and repository enforcement still live only as EOS-018 planning work, so S8 independent approval is not yet encoded in CONTRIBUTING.md or the PR template.
Per-ticket S7 plus S8 Grok load on the 22 grandfathered OBX tickets is bounded but still expensive; it depends on EOS-012 packet-class budgets being frozen before heavy S7 use.

strengths: Exact pin x-ai/grok-4.6 is preserved as mandatory review input on each named S-stage, bounded ticket-readiness packet, PR packet, and release candidate.
PASS/REVISE/BLOCKED are labels on review input; named human owner and independent verifier are the only acceptance voices.
Anti-recursion: do not audit audits or disposition memos; re-audit only on hash-set change; Page IR uses scoped S7/S8 packets.

Hash-first packet with 25-file / 60k prompt / 20k completion budget, split-don't-truncate, and a cross-section packet that must enumerate domain-packet hashes and test authority, data-flow, security, lifecycle, and release interactions.
Fail closed on reported-model mismatch, missing hashes/files, data-class violation, or unavailability; no informal skip or substitute model for ordinary work.
Identical hash sets reuse the stored audit; deliberate same-hash reruns preserve both results for human reconciliation.
P0/P1 closure now requires correction evidence or a documented false-positive/not-applicable ruling accepted by the owner and the required independent verifier; silent risk acceptance is not closure.
Grok cannot close its own P0/P1 findings; failed deterministic tests, schema/security oracles, and named-human visual/evidence/release decisions override a favorable Grok label.

Permanent-withdrawal path now exists: freeze product work; owner plus independent verifier may authorize one governance-only pin-succession packet that names a successor and contains no product implementation, release, provider, or scope decision; successor retrospectively audits that packet; not an ordinary-ticket bypass.
Emergency path remains limited to a pre-accepted rollback/runbook, retrospective audit, and no new feature scope.
Usage/cost recorded against EOS-012; EOS-005 owns the external-model audit channel.
weaknesses: Same model still reviews every layer; independence is only human owner plus independent verifier, which is acceptable under the owner's pin but remains a correlated-review residual.
Pin-succession freeze-lift timing is implicit: the text does not say product work stays frozen until the successor retrospective audit is dispositioned with no unresolved P0/P1.

The prohibition on a 'provider' decision inside the pin-succession packet could be misread as blocking the successor model pin itself; surrounding governance-only and no-scope-decision language contain that risk but should be read as product/hosting/appointment vendors.
Split domain packets plus one cross-section packet can still miss cross-domain interactions if the cross-section is under-scoped.
requiredControls: Keep mandatory exact x-ai/grok-4.6 audit on each named S-stage, bounded ticket packet, PR packet, and RC; do not delete the pin.
Treat Grok output as review_input only; owner decision and independent verifier remain the only acceptance/release voices.
Retain hash-first bounded packets, reported-model fail-closed, same-hash reuse, no audit-of-audits, and no silent truncation.
Retain data-class denylist, hash-only media, restricted raw-store, 90-day default deletion, and EOS-005 ownership of this egress channel.
Retain deterministic tests / schema oracles / named-human visual-evidence-release override over any Grok label.
Keep pin-succession limited to confirmed permanent withdrawal, owner-plus-independent-verifier authorization, governance-only scope, successor retrospective audit, and no ordinary-ticket skip.
Read 'no provider decision' in the succession packet as no product/hosting/appointment vendor selection; the packet may name only the successor audit-model pin.
Keep product work frozen through successor retrospective-audit disposition with no unresolved P0/P1; do not treat authorization alone as unfreeze.
Keep P0/P1 disposition as correction evidence or documented false-positive/not-applicable ruling, never silent risk acceptance, with independent verifier on high-risk boundaries.

priorFindingClosure.reason: No regression. DoR/DoD still require an exact Grok 4.6 receipt, owner disposition, and no unresolved P0/P1 rather than a model PASS certificate. Packets remain hash-first and budgeted; identical hashes reuse receipts; reported-model mismatch and unavailability fail closed; Grok cannot close Grok P0/P1; emergency rollback is narrow; tests and humans outrank the model. Pin-succession is now an explicit governance exception, not a reopened certificate path.

No regression. §6 still denies secrets, env, sites/, .one-box/, OAuth, credentials, raw uploads, browser storage, recordings, and client-identifying evidence; binaries are hash/metadata; repo artifacts are Public or Internal-Redacted; raw payloads are restricted-store with 90-day default deletion. EOS-005 still includes the external-model audit channel and audit-receipt access.

No regression. §2 still splits confirmed versioned-repository inputs from time-specific live observations that are not planning-policy authority and are not used for gap severity. The 22-ticket count now matches docs/tickets/page-ir-safe-pipeline/manifest.json. Live 1,275-test/worktree/GitHub claims remain unavailable in this packet and are listed under evidenceMissing rather than treated as false.

No regression. §5 mapping table and grandfather rule still connect S0–S11 to the program, P1–P8, A0–A4, draft E0–E8, existing OBX tickets, and section 10. S7–S11 are not in force as implementation permission. EOS-018 still names the contribution-control follow-up after owner acceptance.

No regression. EOS-017 still covers A4/GSAP and EVAL-WEB-001/named-human visual qualification; EOS-002/EOS-019 keep draft vendor names as candidates and appointment implementation unauthorized; EOS-018 covers independent-review enforcement; EOS-012 includes Grok audit budget by packet class; EOS-001 names the fail-closed authority/link oracle and keeps AGENTS.md/README.md as entry points until it exists; §9 still labels blocked-domain rows as planning oracles only.

EOS-003 now states that EOS-015 owns the matching capability matrix and that both closures must cite the same Release 1 version. EOS-005 now states that EOS-013 owns operational handoff/offboarding and must implement the same retention, deletion, and export contract. That is the same parent-to-child coupling already accepted for EOS-002→EOS-010. Reverse pointers on EOS-015/EOS-013 are unnecessary once ownership and shared-contract rules are explicit.

§6 now adds a confirmed-permanent-withdrawal path: freeze product work; owner and independent verifier may authorize one governance-only pin-succession packet that names a successor and may contain no product implementation, release, provider, or scope decision; the successor retrospectively audits that exact packet; this is not an ordinary-ticket bypass. Ordinary unavailability still fails closed with wait/stop and the narrow pre-accepted emergency rollback. Residual freeze-lift timing and 'provider' wording are P3 clarity, not a remaining catch-22.

§2 now says Page IR has a machine-readable 22-ticket dependency pack. docs/tickets/page-ir-safe-pipeline/manifest.json contains exactly 22 ticket objects (OBX-001, OBX-002, OBX-010–015, OBX-020–025, OBX-029–031, OBX-040–042, OBX-050–051).
